title: Localized degree-minus-one boundaries are null-homotopies
statement: Let $C$ be a category with Grothendieck topology $J$, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $U$ an object of $C$, and $L,I$ arbitrary integer-indexed cochain complexes of module sheaves. Write $S$ for the abelian-group complex of sections at $U$ of the Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex], with its specified projections $\pi$. Assume that restriction to $C/U$ preserves zero morphisms, and write $\mathrm{res}$ for termwise restriction. For a cycle $z\in Z^0(S)$ and a chain map $f:\mathrm{res}(L)\to\mathrm{res}(I)$, assume that, for every integer $p$ and every object $W$ of $(C/U)^{\mathrm{op}}$, the component $f^p$ evaluated at $W$ equals the evaluation at $W$ of $\pi_{0,p,p}(\iota z)$ at $U$. Then $f$ is null-homotopic if and only if there exists $x\in S^{-1}$ with $\mathrm{toCycles}(x)=z$. This concerns one cycle and one chain map and assumes no equivalence between all cycles and all maps.

proof.text: Apply the Hom-complex product specification from homComplex_exists. Forget sheaves of modules, evaluate at U, and forget to types; these functors preserve the integer-indexed product. Lift each localized presheaf morphism to a sheaf morphism via its Hom constructor. The resulting map c_n from degree-n sections to Mathlib HomComplex.Cochain is bijective: injectivity follows from the limiting fan hom_ext, and a cochain gives a cone with point PUnit whose lift supplies its preimage. This is proved in the private boundaryComparison helper for an arbitrary complex with the specified projections.

Apply the specified projection identity in degrees -1 and 0, simplify (-1).negOnePow to -1, and evaluate the identity on x at U. Restriction has the same underlying component maps. Mathlib HomComplex.δ_v gives the identical sum of postcomposition by d_I and precomposition by d_L, hence c_0(d(x))=δ(-1,0)(c_{-1}(x)).

The assumed component identity implies c_0(iCycles(z))=Cochain.ofHom(f), by degree-zero cochain extensionality and sheaf/presheaf morphism extensionality. HomologicalComplex.toCycles_i evaluated on x gives iCycles(toCycles(x))=d(x).

For a null-homotopy h of f, take a preimage x of Cochain.ofHomotopy(h) using the degree-minus-one bijection. Mathlib δ_ofHomotopy, the differential comparison, and the component identity give c_0(d(x))=c_0(iCycles(z)). Injectivity of c_0 and of the monomorphism iCycles yield toCycles(x)=z. Conversely, a boundary witness x gives Cochain.ofHom(f)=δ(-1,0)(c_{-1}(x)); apply Mathlib Cochain.equivHomotopy(f,0) in reverse. This treats all complexes without boundedness hypotheses, including zero complexes and zero differentials.

lean.statement:
theorem localizedHomComplex_nullHomotopy_iff_boundary
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max u v}) (U : C)
    (L I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{max u v}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R)) ℤ)
    (hzero : Functor.PreservesZeroMorphisms
      (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{max u v}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R) U)) :
    let R₀ := (sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R
    let H := homComplex (R := R) L I
    let π := Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec
      (homComplex_exists.{u, v, max u v, max u v} (J := J) (R := R)))
    let S := ((SheafOfModules.forget R₀ ⋙ PresheafOfModules.evaluation R₀.obj (op U) ⋙
      forget₂ (ModuleCat.{max u v} (R₀.obj.obj (op U))) AddCommGrpCat).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj H
    let := hzero
    let res : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{max u v} R₀) ℤ ⥤
        CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{max u v} (R₀.over U)) ℤ :=
      (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{max u v} R₀ U).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
    ∀ (z : S.cycles 0) (f : res.obj L ⟶ res.obj I),
      (∀ (p : ℤ) (W : (Over U)ᵒᵖ),
        (f.f p).val.app W =
          (((π L I 0 p p (add_zero p)).val.app (op U)) (S.iCycles 0 z)).app W) →
      (Nonempty (Homotopy f 0) ↔ ∃ x : S.X (-1), S.toCycles (-1) 0 x = z)
